Flow: Communal trusts and charitable funds (BPP and others). Stated purpose: The stated purpose is housing, healthcare, education and welfare.. How it controls: Access is conditioned on communal standing and marriage choices, so benevolence works as boundary enforcement.. Who benefits: Trust boards benefit and, genuinely, so do community members in need..

Flow: Housing colonies (baugs). Stated purpose: The stated purpose is affordable community housing.. How it controls: Subsidized housing is withheld from those who marry out, which is the most concrete exit penalty here.. Who benefits: The trust boards that control allocation benefit..

Flow: Ritual and funerary fees. Stated purpose: The stated purpose is priestly services.. How it controls: The priesthood is hereditary and limited in numbers, and funerary access is community-controlled.. Who benefits: Priestly families and trusts benefit..

Flow: Endowment investment income. Stated purpose: The stated purpose is perpetual community support.. How it controls: Large historic endowments are governed by small elected boards whose legitimacy is contested.. Who benefits: Board members and their constituencies benefit..
